calls.title: Pictime & GrowthBook Proposal Discussion
calls.summary: The team discussed strategies to leverage GrowthBook for improving subscription conversions, particularly from free to the beginner paying tier, which currently has a 23% conversion rate among 7,000–8,000 monthly sign-ups. Amir emphasized the importance of optimizing user experience within the app, while James suggested running 10 to 20 experiments monthly to achieve a meaningful conversion lift of 0.5% to 6%. The integration of GrowthBook with Databricks was highlighted for automated analytics and metric tracking, facilitating real-time results without the need for manual analysis. Product managers will benefit from a visual editor and Figma integration, allowing independent experimentation without heavy engineering input. Finally, pricing options were discussed, proposing a no-cost proof of concept in July to assess the platform’s value before commitment.
calls.keywords: A/B Testing, Experimentation, Databricks Integration, Product Analytics, Visual Editor, Conversion Optimization
calls.action_items:
**Gill Matz**
Develop initial metrics in Databricks relevant to the experiments planned for the GrowthBook trial (46:00)

**Tal Binyamini**
Coordinate internal resources for experiment setup and participate in the Monday 11:00 AM kickoff call to align on metric setup and onboarding (46:00)

**James Shannon**
Provide product training and onboarding resources to PicTime team, schedule the follow-up kickoff call on Monday, and extend the free trial through the end of July (34:50)

**Amir Karby**
Evaluate GrowthBook platform during the trial period, discuss contract options with the team, and decide on commitment after proof of concept (33:20)

**Tal Binyamini & Gill Matz**
Continue building partial experiment integration and refine metrics to maximize effective use of GrowthBook features (28:40)

calls.title: Pictime & GrowthBook Commercial Discussion
calls.summary: The meeting centered on solidifying a commercial agreement between GrowthBook and Pictime, confirming a pricing structure of $36,000 annually for 5 seats with additional options. Pictime expressed a preference for quarterly payments with a 3-month exit option to evaluate the platform. A 3-month paid trial was proposed to build usage confidence before committing to an annual contract. Technical integration concerns were discussed, particularly regarding embedding GrowthBook’s SDK within Pictime's existing systems. Pictime was cautiously optimistic about the platform's fit but required proof of its capabilities. Both parties were aligned on the necessity of the trial to establish confidence before entering a longer-term agreement.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, Pictime, Pricing Negotiation, Quarterly Payment, SDK Compatibility, Iframe Integration
